ai.literal: Eyes themselves weeping why indeed? Unceasing pain they to show we saw.
ai.translation: Why do my eyes weep now? It was they who showed him to me, bringing on this unceasing pain that I suffer.
ai.modern: தீராத இந்த காதல் நோயை என் கண்கள் தாமே எனக்குக் காட்டி நான் அதைக் கண்டேன்; அப்படியிருக்க, இப்போது அந்தக் கண்கள் தாமே அழுவது ஏனோ?
ai.explanation: The heroine playfully blames her own eyes for her lovesickness. She points out that her eyes were the ones that first looked at her lover, causing her this unceasing pain. Since they are responsible for bringing about this suffering, she wonders why they are now shedding tears as if they are the victims. The word 'தண்டா' emphasizes that the pain of love is relentless and unceasing.

ai.literal: Having considered without realizing, the painted eyes which looked, having grieved without realizing, suffering sorrow is why?
ai.translation: My painted eyes looked at him without considering the consequences. Why do they now suffer in sorrow, grieving without realizing it is their own fault?
ai.modern: பின்னால் வரும் துன்பத்தை ஆராய்ந்து உணராமல் அன்று காதலரை நோக்கிய என் மை தீட்டிய கண்கள், இன்று தாங்களே செய்த பிழையை உணராமல் வருந்தித் துன்பப்படுவது ஏன்?
ai.explanation: The speaker questions the current sorrow of her own eyes, which are weeping from the pain of separation. She notes the irony that these painted eyes eagerly looked at her lover without realizing the future pain of parting. Now, they suffer deep sorrow, grieving without realizing that they themselves caused this misery by looking at him in the first place. The repetition of the word 'உணரா' (without realizing) emphasizes the eyes' lack of foresight then and their lack of self-awareness now.

ai.literal: Swiftly having looked themselves, they themselves weep; this to laugh fit thing possesses.
ai.translation: My eyes eagerly looked at him themselves, and now they themselves weep. This situation is truly fit to be laughed at.
ai.modern: விரைந்து சென்று தாமே அவரைப் பார்த்துவிட்டு, இப்போது தாமே அழுகின்ற என் கண்களின் இந்த நிலைமை சிரிக்கத் தக்கதாக இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks about her pining eyes, pointing out the irony of their situation. She notes that her eyes eagerly sought out her lover on their own, but now they are the ones weeping because of his absence. The word 'கதுமென' means swiftly or eagerly, highlighting their initial haste. She concludes that this self-inflicted suffering possesses a nature ('உடைத்து') that is fit only to be laughed at ('நகத் தக்கது').

ai.literal: weeping unable tears dried-up painted-eyes surviving not-allowing escape-without disease in-me having-placed
ai.translation: My painted eyes, their tears dried up and unable to weep, have inflicted upon me an inescapable disease that does not let me survive.
ai.modern: அழ முடியாமல் கண்ணீர் வற்றிப்போன என் மை தீட்டிய கண்கள், நான் பிழைக்க முடியாதபடி தப்பிக்க வழியில்லாத ஒரு நோயை எனக்குள் நிலைநிறுத்திவிட்டன.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments the state of her eyes, which have wept so much for her absent lover that they have run out of tears. Now, unable to weep and completely dried up, they have inflicted a cureless, fatal pain upon her. The word 'நிறுத்து' (having placed) acts as the finite verb, showing how the eyes, which are supposed to be a part of her, have acted independently to establish this inescapable disease ('உய்வில் நோய்') within her.

ai.literal: Unable to close, sorrow suffer, sea uncontainable love-sickness caused my eyes.
ai.translation: My eyes, which caused this love-sickness vaster than the ocean, now suffer in sorrow, unable to close in sleep.
ai.modern: கடலை விடப் பெரியதான இந்தக் காதல் நோயை எனக்கு உண்டாக்கிய என் கண்கள், இப்போது தூங்க முடியாமல் துன்பப்படுகின்றன.
ai.explanation: The speaker blames her own eyes for her immense suffering. It was her eyes that first looked at her lover, bringing upon her a love-sickness that is vaster than the ocean. Now, in a fitting turn of events, those very eyes are unable to close in sleep and are suffering in sorrow. The couplet beautifully captures the irony of the eyes being both the cause of the passion and the victims of its resulting sleeplessness.

ai.explanation: The speaker is suffering from the pain of lovesickness and is unable to sleep. She realizes that her eyes are the ones that first looked at her lover and brought this affliction upon her. Seeing her eyes now continuously weeping and sharing in the suffering, she feels a sense of poetic justice. The exclamation 'Oh!' and the word 'sweet' highlight her playful satisfaction that the culprits are facing the consequences of their own action.

ai.literal: Suffering, suffering, let the inner water dry up, having desired, having melted, having wanted, the eyes that saw him.
ai.translation: My eyes eagerly desired, melted, and begged to see him; now let them suffer and weep until their tears run dry.
ai.modern: அவரைப் பார்க்க வேண்டும் என்று விரும்பி, மனம் உருகி, வேண்டி நின்ற என் கண்கள், இப்போது அவரைப் பிரிந்து அழுது அழுது தமக்குள்ளே இருக்கும் கண்ணீர் வற்றும் அளவுக்குத் துன்பப்படட்டும்.
ai.explanation: The heroine addresses her own eyes, which are now weeping constantly because her lover is away. She reminds them that it was they who eagerly desired, melted, and begged to see him in the first place. Therefore, she says, let them now suffer the consequences of their own actions and weep until their tears completely dry up. The repetition of 'உழந்து' (suffering) emphasizes the intensity of the pain, while the sequence of 'விழைந்து இழைந்து வேண்டி' captures the escalating eagerness of the eyes before they saw him.

ai.explanation: The heroine laments the state of her eyes, which long to see her lover. She notes the irony that the man who once desired her now shows no care for her suffering, yet her eyes refuse to rest until they see him. The word 'பேணாது' (without caring) contrasts with 'பெட்டார்' (he who loved), highlighting his changed attitude, while 'அமைவு இல' (have no peace) shows her eyes' uncontrollable longing.

ai.literal: If comes not, sleep not; if comes, sleep not; in that state, intense sorrow have experienced eyes.
ai.translation: If he does not come, my eyes do not sleep; if he comes, they still do not sleep. In either case, my eyes endure intense sorrow.
ai.modern: அவர் வராதபோதும் என் கண்கள் தூங்குவதில்லை; அவர் வந்தாலும் தூங்குவதில்லை. ஆக இந்த இரண்டு நிலைகளிலும் என் கண்கள் தாங்க முடியாத துன்பத்தையே அடைகின்றன.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments the restless state of her eyes, which are caught in a paradox of longing and love. If her lover is away, her eyes cannot sleep because they are anxiously waiting and weeping for his return. If he is present, they still cannot sleep because they are too captivated by him and fear losing sight of him even for a moment. Thus, in both situations, her eyes are condemned to experience intense, inescapable sorrow.

ai.literal: Secret obtaining to townspeople difficult is not indeed, our like beaten drum eyes-who-have inside.
ai.translation: It is not difficult for the townspeople to discover the secrets within those whose eyes, like ours, beat like a drum.
ai.modern: எம்மைப் போலப் பறை அறைந்து செய்தியைச் சொல்லும் கண்களை உடையவர்களின் மனத்தில் உள்ள ரகசியத்தை அறிவது ஊராருக்குக் கடினமான செயல் அல்ல.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments that her eyes are betraying her hidden sorrow. She compares her eyes to a beaten drum (அறை பறை) that loudly announces news to the whole town. The word அறை has multiple meanings such as a room or a rock, but here it means beaten or sounding, fitting the drum metaphor. Because her eyes weep and show her inner feelings so openly, it is not difficult (அரிது அன்று) for the townspeople to discover the secret (மறை) kept inside (அகத்து) her heart.
